detailed_rationale:
CRISIL is India's leading credit-rating, research, and analytics group, majority-owned by S&P Global (66.6% promoter holding), operating in an effectively oligopolistic domestic ratings market (essentially a 3-player structure with ICRA and CARE). The fundamentals here are excellent by any standard: ROE ~27% (3-year average), ROCE ~33%, consistent revenue growth of 15-18% YoY in the most recent quarters (Jun-2026: Rs.1,075 Cr sales, Rs.216 Cr profit), FY25 annual sales of Rs.3,649 Cr (+12%) and profit of Rs.766 Cr (+12%) with a 30% operating margin, and a 57% dividend payout ratio -- a genuinely high-quality, cash-generative, wide-moat compounder. The Ratings segment alone generates 51% of total group profit from just 28% of revenue, underscoring the pricing power of the core licensed-rating-agency business.

Our own scored dataset, however, shows this name as zero_cov_flag = True with numerous key fields blank -- market cap, ROE, ROCE, debt/equity, 3-year revenue CAGR, quality score, and value score are all empty in our CSV, and coverage is flagged only 'Med' even on the 3-year view. Given the externally-verified fundamentals are unambiguously strong (high ROE/ROCE, consistent double-digit growth, oligopoly moat, high payout), we believe the Sell classification for this specific name is very likely an artifact of these data gaps rather than a genuine reflection of weak fundamentals -- the scoring engine simply did not have the inputs to credit this business properly.

Valuation (P/E ~36.4x, P/B ~9.84x) is full, consistent with the quality of the franchise, and 10-year sales/profit CAGR of 10% each suggests durable but moderate (not spectacular) long-run growth tied to India's credit and capital-market activity. Reverse-DCF: a ~36x multiple for a 30%+ ROCE oligopoly business with a 10%+ growth track record is a fair, not obviously cheap or rich, price -- this is a case of paying a full price for a genuinely excellent business, which is a defensible Hold rather than a Sell.
recommendation_rationale: We are rescuing the quant Sell to Hold, because the externally-verified fundamentals (ROE 27%, ROCE 33%, an oligopoly moat, consistent double-digit growth, 57% payout) are unambiguously strong and inconsistent with a Sell classification, and our own dataset flags this specific name as zero_cov_flag=True with the majority of scoring inputs (ROE, ROCE, D/E, 3-year revenue CAGR, quality score, value score) blank. We separately escalate the underlying data-coverage gap, since it may be a systemic issue affecting other zero_cov_flag names across the 750-stock universe, not unique to CRISIL.
summary: CRISIL is India's leading credit-rating and research group, majority-owned by S&P Global, operating in an effectively 3-player domestic ratings oligopoly. Return on equity (~27%) and return on capital (~33%) are excellent, revenue has grown a consistent 12-18% across recent periods, and the group pays out over half its profit as dividends. At roughly 36 times earnings, the stock is fully priced for this quality but not obviously expensive relative to it. Our internal quantitative data for this name has significant coverage gaps, which we believe explains the Sell signal more than the underlying business quality. We rate this a Hold and are separately flagging the data-coverage gap for review.
positive_para: An oligopoly-moat business (effectively a 3-player domestic ratings market) with ROE ~27%, ROCE ~33%, 12-18% recent revenue growth, a highly profitable core Ratings segment (51% of profit from 28% of revenue), and a 57% dividend payout ratio -- genuinely excellent, cash-generative fundamentals by any standard.
negative_para: Valuation is full (~36x earnings, ~9.8x book), and long-run (10-year) growth of 10% CAGR, while durable, is not spectacular -- the business's growth is tied to India's credit and capital-market issuance activity, which is cyclical. Our internal quant dataset for this specific name has unusually large coverage gaps (zero_cov_flag=True, several key fields blank), which we treat as a data-quality caveat rather than a business-quality concern, but it does mean our own scoring could not properly evaluate this name.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~36x earnings for a 30%+ ROCE oligopoly business with a 10-18% growth track record and high payout, the price is full but fair -- not a bargain, but not disconnected from the demonstrated quality either.
escalation_reason: CRISIL is flagged zero_cov_flag=True in our scored universe with market_cap, ROE, ROCE, debt_equity, revenue_cagr_3y, quality_score, and value_score all blank, yet externally-verified fundamentals (ROE ~27%, ROCE ~33%, consistent double-digit growth, oligopoly moat) are clearly strong. This looks like a genuine methodology gap -- names with zero_cov_flag=True may be receiving unreliable composite Sell/Hold scores purely because required inputs are missing, not because the underlying business is weak. Recommend a system-wide check of how zero_cov_flag/blank-field names are scored across the full 750-stock universe, since this could be mis-classifying other genuinely high-quality names besides CRISIL.
